title: Dell FY2026 Q4 results
summary: Dell FY26 closed more than $64B in AI-optimized server orders, shipped more than $25B, entered FY27 with a $43B backlog, and guided FY27 AI-optimized server revenue to roughly $50B, up 103% year over year.

title: Micron FY2025 results
summary: Micron FY2025 revenue was $37.378B, GAAP gross margin was 39.8%, operating cash flow was $17.53B, adjusted free cash flow was $3.72B and net capex was $13.80B.

title: Micron FY2025 Q4 prepared remarks
summary: Micron said combined HBM, high-capacity DIMM and low-power server DRAM revenue reached $10B in FY2025, more than five times the prior fiscal year.

title: Micron FY2026 Q1 results
summary: Micron FY26 Q1 delivered record revenue and margin expansion, with AI data-center memory demand driving cloud memory and HBM-related strength.

title: Micron FY2026 Q1 prepared remarks
summary: Micron prepared remarks forecast HBM TAM from about $35B in calendar 2025 to around $100B in calendar 2028, about 40% CAGR, and said 2026 HBM supply had completed price and volume agreements.

title: NVIDIA FY2026 Q4 results
summary: NVIDIA Q4 FY26 revenue was $68.1B and Data Center revenue was $62.3B, up 75% YoY. FY2026 revenue was $215.9B, GAAP gross margin was 71.1%, operating income was $130.4B and free cash flow was $96.6B. Q1 FY27 revenue outlook was $78.0B +/-2% with no China Data Center compute revenue assumed.

title: NVIDIA platform HBM specification progression
summary: NVIDIA platform specifications show H100 at 80GB HBM, H200 at 141GB, Blackwell at 192GB, Blackwell Ultra at 288GB and Rubin at up to 288GB HBM4 with up to 22TB/s bandwidth.

title: SemiAnalysis AI Capacity Constraints CoWoS and HBM Supply Chain
summary: SemiAnalysis identified CoWoS and HBM as AI accelerator bottlenecks and explained CoWoS as TSMC 2.5D packaging that integrates logic and HBM on an interposer.

title: Samsung Q4 and FY2025 results
summary: Samsung Q4 2025 Memory Business reached record quarterly revenue and operating profit, with HBM, server DDR5 and enterprise SSD as high-value AI products.

title: Samsung commercial HBM4 shipment
summary: Samsung announced commercial HBM4 shipments, described stable initial mass-production yields, expected 2026 HBM sales to more than triple versus 2025 and said it was expanding HBM4 capacity.

title: SK hynix FY2024 results
summary: SK hynix FY2024 revenue was KRW66.1930T, operating profit KRW23.4673T and operating margin 35%; HBM exceeded 40% of DRAM revenue in Q4 2024.

title: SK hynix FY2025 results
summary: SK hynix FY2025 revenue was KRW97.1467T, operating profit KRW47.2063T and operating margin 49%, driven by AI memory and HBM leadership.

title: TrendForce Blackwell Ultra and B200A HBM3e 12hi Consumption
summary: TrendForce described NVIDIA as the largest HBM buyer, expected procurement share above 70%, with HBM consumption growing more than 200% in 2024 and expected to double again in 2025 as Blackwell raises HBM content.

title: TrendForce HBM Market Bulletin February 2026
summary: TrendForce assessed Samsung as leading HBM4 validation, SK hynix as retaining volume leadership and Micron as slightly behind, while NVIDIA was expected to use all three suppliers under tight capacity.

title: TrendForce HBM Market Bulletin March 2026
summary: TrendForce said stricter HBM4 specifications delayed supplier validation, creating downside risk to early HBM4 shipments and next-generation AI platform timing; unmet HBM4 demand could shift back to HBM3E.

title: TrendForce HBM Industry Analysis 4Q25
summary: TrendForce said SK hynix led with about 150K TSV capacity; yield, certification and backend capacity constrained near-term supply; all three suppliers planned HBM4 mass production in 2026.

title: TrendForce HBM Prices to Increase by 5-10% in 2025
summary: TrendForce estimated HBM ASP at several times conventional DRAM and about five times DDR5, while value share could exceed 30% of DRAM in 2025.

title: TrendForce HBM supplier share outlook
summary: TrendForce-related public reporting projected SK hynix global HBM bit output share at 59% in 2025 and 50% in 2026, while Samsung could rise from 20% to 28%; these are forecasts rather than audited actual shares.
